chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Is there an obligatory prayer for the Ziyarah of the Grave?' He replied, 'There is no obligatory prayer for it.' I asked him, 'On how many days should one go for Ziyarah?' He replied, 'As much as you wish.'
ai.seo_question: Is there a specific obligatory prayer or fixed frequency for visiting the grave in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that while Ziyarah is a highly recommended act of devotion, it does not carry the weight of an obligatory (fard) prayer, distinguishing it from core ritual duties. The Imam’s response, 'Do as you please,' underscores the flexibility and voluntary nature of the practice, encouraging believers to visit the graves of the Ahl al-Bayt (a.s.) according to their capacity and spiritual inclination without the burden of a strict minimum or maximum limit.
